correctness.rationale: The n-rung bipartite ladder alternating matrix splits into an unrestricted n-by-n tridiagonal block and its negative transpose, so skew rank is twice tridiagonal rank. Kernel dimension is propagated one equation at a time; the 5 possible types of 2D boundary image reduce to 4 because vertical and oblique lines have the same aggregate transitions. Explicit enumeration of each row type yields the displayed row vector, 4x4 matrix and final column, including the independent terminal dummy variable. The ordinary group-character factor is obtained by decomposing the twisted group algebra over each central character of odd-characteristic class-two graphical groups. The included checker independently exhausts all tridiagonal matrices in 12 small test cases and actual alternating graph matrices in 6, including a nonprime field; a separate nonsingular recurrence check agrees with a published determinant count. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove the unrestricted theorem.

originality.rationale: The graph-to-tridiagonal equivalence converts the desired character-degree formula into a rank census for independent tridiagonal entries. The source comparisons distinguish a general support-pattern framework (Lewis et al.), a generic character problem and rank reduction (Rossmann), a determinant/full-rank tridiagonal count (Jitman–Sricharoen), and graph-Lie algebra construction (Mainkar) from the specific all-rank fixed four-state ladder transfer. The source search did not find the same transfer or a theorem implying all its coefficients. Published tree/cycle/bouquet/coning cases are narrower or structurally different; the n=2 boundary and nonsingular term are expressly not claimed new. A more general yet unlocated transfer theorem is a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: A broadly formulated bounded-pathwidth/zero-pattern rank-transfer theorem absent from the targeted searches could subsume the matrix recurrence.

value.rationale: The ladder is a canonical non-tree, noncycle, 2-connected family with unboundedly many cycles. All ordinary character degree counts for its class-two graphical groups were specifically motivated by Rossmann’s open enumeration question; a transfer of fixed dimension four over Z[q,z] evaluates every rank cell and thus every degree population in arbitrary ladder length and odd field size. This gives structural arithmetic data not contained in the previous determinant/nonsingularity census, and is not a routine substitution of a tree/cycle/amalgamation recurrence.
